jp: カーテンを{開[あ]けると/開[あ]けたら|cd-to}、まぶしい光[ひかり]が部屋[へや]に入[はい]ってきた。
en: When I opened the curtains, bright sunlight streamed into the room.
why: An action followed by a past discovery or event is linked with と (たら also works); ば and なら cannot report a past event.

jp: 台所[だいどころ]に{行[い]くと/行[い]ったら|cd-to}、母[はは]が朝[あさ]ごはんを作[つく]っていた。
en: When I went into the kitchen, my mother was making breakfast.
why: Going somewhere and finding something is a past discovery, which takes と or たら, never ば or なら.

jp: 子[こ]ども部屋[べや]を{のぞくと/のぞいたら|cd-to}、弟[おとうと]はまだ寝[ね]ていた。
en: When I looked into the kids' room, my little brother was still asleep.
why: What one finds on looking in is a past discovery, so と (or たら) is used.

jp: この古[ふる]い家[いえ]は、冬[ふゆ]に{なると/なれば|cd-to}、廊下[ろうか]がとても冷[つめ]たくなります。
en: In winter, the hallway of this old house gets very cold.
why: A natural, repeated result of a season arriving is expressed with と; なら and ても do not fit.

jp: 洗濯機[せんたくき]のボタンを{押[お]すと/押[お]せば|cd-to}、自動[じどう]で水[みず]が入[はい]ります。
en: When you press the button on the washing machine, water goes in automatically.
why: A button press followed automatically by its result is the classic と pattern; なら and ても break the cause-effect link.

jp: 家[いえ]を{出[で]ると/出[で]たら|cd-to}、すぐ目[め]の前[まえ]に小[ちい]さな公園[こうえん]があります。
en: As soon as you leave the house, there is a small park right in front of you.
why: One step leads straight to the next thing you see, so と is right; なら would mean 'if you are leaving' and ても 'even if'.

jp: 子[こ]どものころ、夜[よる]に{なると|cd-to}、祖母[そぼ]がいつも昔話[むかしばなし]をしてくれた。
en: When I was a child, whenever night came, my grandmother always told me old tales.
why: A habitual 'whenever X, Y happened' is expressed with と; なら and ても would change the meaning.

jp: 朝[あさ]起[お]きて窓[まど]の外[そと]を{見[み]ると/見[み]たら|cd-to}、庭[にわ]が真[ま]っ白[しろ]だった。
en: When I looked out the window after getting up, the garden was all white.
why: Looking and discovering a past fact calls for と or たら; ば and なら cannot introduce a discovery.

jp: 家[いえ]に{帰[かえ]ると/帰[かえ]ったら|cd-to}、玄関[げんかん]に大[おお]きな荷物[にもつ]が置[お]いてあった。
en: When I got home, a big package had been left at the front door.
why: Coming home and finding something is a past discovery, so と or たら; なら would mean 'if you are going home'.

jp: 夜中[よなか]に目[め]が{覚[さ]めると/覚[さ]めたら|cd-to}、隣[となり]で妹[いもうと]が泣[な]いていた。
en: When I woke up in the middle of the night, my little sister was crying next to me.
why: Waking up and finding something is a past discovery; ば and なら cannot report it.

jp: 家族[かぞく]みんなでテレビを{見[み]ていると/見[み]ていたら|cd-to}、突然[とつぜん]停電[ていでん]になった。
en: While the whole family was watching TV, the power suddenly went out.
why: An unexpected event that occurs during an ongoing action is linked with ていると (ていたら also works).

jp: 母[はは]の料理[りょうり]は、{食[た]べれば|cd-ba}食[た]べるほど、もっと食[た]べたくなります。
en: The more of my mother's cooking I eat, the more I want to eat.
why: The 'the more ~, the more ~' pattern is built only with the ば form repeated before ほど.

jp: 家[いえ]は{広[ひろ]ければ|cd-ba}広[ひろ]いほど、掃除[そうじ]が大変[たいへん]です。
en: The bigger a house is, the harder it is to clean.
why: X ば X ほど needs the ば form of the adjective: 広ければ広いほど.

jp: 今朝[けさ]は眠[ねむ]い。昨日[きのう]もっと早[はや]く{寝[ね]れば/寝[ね]たら|cd-ba}よかった。
en: I'm sleepy this morning. I should have gone to bed earlier last night.
why: Regret about something not done is expressed with ばよかった (たらよかった also works); と and なら do not form it.

jp: {よければ/よかったら|cd-ba}、夕[ゆう]ごはんを一緒[いっしょ]に食[た]べませんか。
en: If it suits you, won't you have dinner with us?
why: A polite invitation uses よければ or よかったら; と cannot be followed by an invitation and ても means 'even if good'.

jp: あと五分[ごふん]{あれば/あったら|cd-ba}、朝[あさ]ごはんが食[た]べられるのに。
en: If I had five more minutes, I could eat breakfast.
why: A wish contrary to fact (のに) takes ば or たら; と and なら cannot express it.

jp: 犬[いぬ]の顔[かお]は、{見[み]れば|cd-ba}見[み]るほど、かわいく思[おも]えてくる。
en: The more I look at the dog's face, the cuter it seems.
why: Only the ば form can be repeated before ほど to mean 'the more ... the more ...'.

jp: 時間[じかん]が{あれば/あったら|cd-ba}、夕飯[ゆうはん]の準備[じゅんび]を手伝[てつだ]います。
en: If I have time, I will help prepare dinner.
why: The main clause states the speaker's intention, which と cannot follow; ば or たら is needed, and ても means 'even if'.

jp: おなかが{すいていれば/すいていたら/すいているなら|cd-ba}、冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]のケーキを食[た]べてもいいよ。
en: If you're hungry, you may eat the cake in the fridge.
why: Granting permission after a condition needs ば or たら; と cannot be followed by permission and ても reverses the logic.

jp: 古[ふる]い家[いえ]でも、{住[す]めば|cd-ba}都[みやこ]と言[い]いますから、すぐ慣[な]れますよ。
en: Even if it's an old house, they say wherever you live becomes home, so you'll get used to it quickly.
why: The set proverb 住めば都 uses the ば form; no other conditional is used in it.

jp: 部屋[へや]は、{片付[かたづ]ければ|cd-ba}片付[かたづ]けるほど、広[ひろ]く感[かん]じられる。
en: The more you tidy a room, the bigger it feels.
why: The ほど pattern needs the repeated ば form: 片付ければ片付けるほど.

jp: 来年[らいねん]、家族[かぞく]が{増[ふ]えれば/増[ふ]えたら|cd-ba}、もっと広[ひろ]い家[いえ]に引[ひ]っ越[こ]したい。
en: If our family grows next year, I want to move to a bigger house.
why: The main clause expresses a wish, so と is impossible; ば or たら fits and ても would mean 'even if'.

jp: 家[いえ]に{帰[かえ]ったら|cd-tara}、すぐ電話[でんわ]してください。
en: When you get home, please call me right away.
why: A request after 'once something is done' takes たら; と cannot precede a request and なら changes the meaning to 'if you are going home'.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]が{終[お]わったら|cd-tara}、テレビを見[み]てもいいですよ。
en: Once your homework is finished, you may watch TV.
why: Permission that follows completion of something is expressed with たら; と cannot lead into permission.

jp: ご飯[はん]を{食[た]べたら|cd-tara}、お皿[さら]を洗[あら]ってね。
en: After you eat, please wash the dishes.
why: 'After finishing X, do Y' as a request uses たら; と cannot take a request and なら would reverse the order.

jp: 大人[おとな]に{なったら/なれば|cd-tara}、自分[じぶん]の家[いえ]を持[も]ちたいです。
en: When I grow up, I want to have a house of my own.
why: A hope tied to a future point in time takes たら; と cannot be followed by a wish and なら or ても change the meaning.

jp: お風呂[ふろ]から{上[あ]がったら|cd-tara}、すぐに髪[かみ]をかわかしなさい。
en: When you get out of the bath, dry your hair right away.
why: A command that follows a completed action takes たら; と cannot precede a command and ても means 'even if'.

jp: 熱[ねつ]があるなら、今日[きょう]は{休[やす]んだら|cd-tara}どうですか。
en: If you have a fever, why don't you take today off?
why: The suggestion pattern is fixed as たらどうですか; ば and なら cannot replace it.

jp: 朝[あさ]、洗濯物[せんたくもの]を{干[ほ]したら/干[ほ]すと|cd-tara}、すぐに雨[あめ]が降[ふ]ってきた。
en: When I hung out the laundry in the morning, it began to rain right away.
why: An unexpected result right after a past action is reported with たら or と; ば and なら cannot report a past event.

jp: もし宝[たから]くじが{当[あ]たったら/当[あ]たれば|cd-tara}、家族[かぞく]みんなで旅行[りょこう]したい。
en: If I won the lottery, I would like to travel with the whole family.
why: A hypothetical event followed by a wish takes たら (or ば); と cannot lead into a wish and ても means 'even if'.

jp: 駅[えき]に{着[つ]いたら|cd-tara}、お母[かあ]さんに知[し]らせてね。
en: When you arrive at the station, let Mom know.
why: A request that follows arrival uses たら; と cannot precede a request and ても means 'even if you arrive'.

jp: 子[こ]どもが{寝[ね]たら/寝[ね]れば|cd-tara}、ゆっくりお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]みたいなあ。
en: Once the kids are asleep, I'd like to drink tea in peace.
why: A wish that depends on something being completed takes たら (or ば); と cannot lead into a wish.

jp: 昨日[きのう]、押[お]し入[い]れを{整理[せいり]したら/整理[せいり]すると|cd-tara}、古[ふる]いアルバムが出[で]てきた。
en: When I sorted through the closet yesterday, an old photo album turned up.
why: A surprising find after a past action is expressed with たら or と, not with ば or なら.

jp: もし雨[あめ]が{降[ふ]ったら/降[ふ]れば|cd-tara}、洗濯物[せんたくもの]はどうしますか。
en: If it rains, what will you do about the laundry?
why: A question about what to do in a hypothetical case takes たら (or ば); と cannot ask for a decision and ても means 'even if'.

jp: これから買[か]い物[もの]に行[い]ってきます。{行[い]くなら|cd-nara}、牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]も買[か]ってきて。
en: "I'm going shopping now." "If you're going, buy some milk too."
why: Responding to what the other person just said ('if, as you say, you are going') uses なら; と and ば cannot lead into a request.

jp: 今夜[こんや]は出[で]かけます。{出[で]かけるなら|cd-nara}、電気[でんき]を消[け]していってね。
en: "I'm going out tonight." "If you're going out, turn off the lights before you leave."
why: The lights are turned off before leaving, so the condition is the planned action itself: 出かけるなら; 出かけたら would put it after leaving.

jp: ケーキを作[つく]りたいんです。{作[つく]るなら|cd-nara}、先[さき]に卵[たまご]を冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]から出[だ]しておくといいよ。
en: "I want to make a cake." "If you're going to make one, take the eggs out of the fridge first."
why: The advice applies before the cake is made, so the condition is the plan itself (なら); 作ったら would mean after it is done.

jp: このへんでおいしいパン屋[や]を知[し]りませんか。パン屋[や]{なら/だったら|cd-nara}、駅前[えきまえ]の店[みせ]がいいですよ。
en: "Do you know a good bakery around here?" "If it's a bakery you want, the shop in front of the station is good."
why: Taking up the topic the other person just raised ('as for a bakery') is the job of なら after a noun.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]は京都[きょうと]がいいかなあ。京都[きょうと]{なら/だったら|cd-nara}、秋[あき]に行[い]くのがおすすめだよ。
en: "I wonder if Kyoto would be good for the trip." "If it's Kyoto, I recommend going in autumn."
why: Commenting on a topic the listener has just named is done with 'noun + なら'; the other options give the wrong logic.

jp: 頭[あたま]が痛[いた]いんです。{痛[いた]いなら/痛[いた]かったら|cd-nara}、薬[くすり]を飲[の]んだほうがいいよ。
en: "I have a headache." "If it hurts, you'd better take some medicine."
why: Giving advice based on what the other person just said uses なら; と cannot lead into advice and ても means 'even if'.

jp: 犬[いぬ]を飼[か]おうかな。{飼[か]うなら|cd-nara}、先[さき]に家族[かぞく]みんなで世話[せわ]の仕方[しかた]を話[はな]し合[あ]おうね。
en: "I'm thinking of getting a dog." "If you're going to get one, let's first talk as a family about how to care for it."
why: '先に' shows the talk comes before getting the dog, so the condition is the plan itself: 飼うなら.

jp: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しを考[かんが]えているんです。{引[ひ]っ越[こ]すなら|cd-nara}、学校[がっこう]に近[ちか]いところがいいね。
en: "I'm thinking about moving." "If you're going to move, somewhere near the school would be good."
why: A judgment about a plan the other person just mentioned takes なら; the other forms do not respond to that plan.

jp: 洗濯[せんたく]をします。{洗濯[せんたく]するなら|cd-nara}、このタオルも一緒[いっしょ]にお願[ねが]い。
en: "I'm going to do the laundry." "If you're doing laundry, please wash this towel too."
why: The towel must go in with the load being started, so the condition is the plan itself (なら), not 'after it is done'.

jp: 明日[あした]は五時[ごじ]に起[お]きるよ。{起[お]きるなら|cd-nara}、今夜[こんや]は早[はや]く寝[ね]たほうがいいね。
en: "I'm getting up at five tomorrow." "If you're getting up then, you'd better go to bed early tonight."
why: Going to bed comes before getting up, so the condition is the plan itself (なら); たら would place the advice after waking.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]、弁当[べんとう]を作[つく]るのが大変[たいへん]なんです。{大変[たいへん]なら/大変[たいへん]だったら|cd-nara}、週[しゅう]に二回[にかい]だけにしたら？
en: "Making a lunch box every morning is hard." "If it's hard, why not do it only twice a week?"
why: Taking the other person's complaint as the premise for a suggestion is the use of なら; the others change the logic.

jp: ふとんに{入[はい]ると/入[はい]れば|cd-to}、すぐに眠[ねむ]くなってしまう。
en: As soon as I get into the futon, I get sleepy.
why: A reliable automatic result of an action is expressed with と; なら and ても would change the meaning.

jp: 今夜[こんや]は寒[さむ]いね。{寒[さむ]いなら/寒[さむ]かったら|cd-nara}、ストーブをつけようか。
en: "It's cold tonight." "If it's cold, shall I turn on the heater?"
why: An offer based on what the other person just said takes なら; と cannot lead into 'shall I' and ても means 'even if'.
